Comment: Thor PAI workflow. Materialises every route by which an account reaches a privileged target. StartRun stages the targets this run recomputes - every matching target for a new or edited definition, otherwise only those the scan's changes can affect. Expand walks the group layer down from each target a level at a time; then waves of a Distributed Map join each staged path to its direct account members and write the routes, and Finalize prunes the routes the run did not re-prove. Started by the scan-completion gate (Thor.ScanGate) with {TenantId, ScanId}. Terraform substitutes the placeholders with templatefile; validate edits with: aws stepfunctions validate-state-machine-definition.

StartRun.Comment: Validates the request, opens the run's workflow row, seeds definitions from config, stages the targets to compute or retire, and hands back the first fan-out wave. The wave is only offsets into paths Expand has yet to stage, so it can be planned here.

Expand.Comment: Stages the simple paths down the group layer from each target, one batched Neptune hop per level. Stops on a time budget and answers IsInProgress; ExpandCheck invokes it again and it resumes from the deepest staged level, which is always a finished one.

ExpandCheck.Comment: No Wait between turns: an in-progress expand has just spent its whole budget working.

FanoutWave.Label: FanoutWave
FanoutWave.Comment: Each item is a window of the run's staged paths - an offset and a limit - and the invocation reads its own rows for it. Items arrive complete from StartRun and NextWave, so there is no ItemSelector: ScanId and RunId are optional, and a reference path that resolves to nothing fails the execution. MaxConcurrency is the connection dial: each body opens a read and a write connection. Results come back inline because NextWave reads the counts. A failed item is tolerated: RecordChunkFailure marks its paths failed, so Finalize never prunes their targets.

Catch.Comment: ResultPath $.Error merges the error into the item, so the next state has both the window that was lost and why.

RecordChunkFailure.Comment: Marks this window's paths failed and appends it to the run's workflow.error before the run moves on without it.

Catch.Comment: Failing to write the record must not fail the run - that would undo the tolerating this state exists to support.

FanoutChunkTolerated.Comment: Wrapped in Payload so the Map's ResultSelector ($[*].Payload) picks a tolerated item up the same way it picks up a successful one.

NextWave.Comment: Sums the paths the wave read: a full wave may be followed by more, a short one ends the loop. Touches no database.

MoreWaves.Comment: The loop. Each turn costs a handful of execution-history events against the 25,000 cap - the answer to a tenant that approaches it is a bigger chunk, not a deeper loop.

Finalize.Comment: Prunes the routes the run was answerable for but did not re-prove, closes the workflow row - completed_with_errors if any chunk was tolerated - and drops the run's staging.

RecordFailure.Comment: Closes the run's workflow row as failed. Here rather than in each step's own try/catch because a Lambda killed by its timeout or by running out of memory runs no catch block. This is the run dying, not a chunk failing - a chunk is tolerated inside the Map.

Catch.Comment: Failing to record the failure must not swallow the failure.

WorkflowFailed.Cause: See the run's workflow row - status 'failed', with the error in the error column. The run's scans stay uncovered, so the next PAI run picks their changes up.
